title: On the Complexity of Level-Synchronized Tree Automata for Quantum Circuit Verification
authors: Michael Blondin, Samy Chady Khoumsi-Kasmi, Guillermo A. Pérez, Marnix Suilen
abstract: Reliable quantum computation requires methods for verifying quantum circuits. Level-synchronized tree automata (LSTAs) were recently introduced to represent sets of quantum states for this purpose. We study LSTAs along two axes relevant to verification: the complexity of their decision problems and the size of their representations under circuit operations. We prove that acyclic LSTAs have NP-complete nonemptiness and $Π_2^P$-complete language inclusion, and that general language inclusion is EXPSPACE-complete. We further prove inherent quadratic representation growth under individual quantum gates in a fixed qubit order, and give an adjacent-qubit reordering construction that preserves level synchronization. These results clarify the scope of applicability of the automata-theoretic toolbox for quantum circuit verification.
summary: This paper investigates the theoretical complexity of using Level-Synchronized Tree Automata (LSTAs) for quantum circuit verification. It proves that key decision problems associated with these automata range from NP-complete to EXPSPACE-complete. The results clarify the inherent computational limits and structural growth rates when applying automata theory to quantum state representation.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the computational complexity of using Level-Synchronized Tree Automata (LSTAs) to verify quantum circuits.
main_result: It establishes that the nonemptiness problem for acyclic LSTAs is NP-complete, while general language inclusion is EXPSPACE-complete.
method: The authors use automata theory, complexity theory reductions (e.g., from satisfiability problems), and structural analysis of gate operations to bound the complexity of LSTA properties.
model_or_system: The model involves representing sets of quantum states using LSTAs, which are defined over perfect binary trees corresponding to $n$-qubit systems. Verification requires transforming the automaton for each quantum gate.
key_observables: The complexity class of the decision problems (e.g., NP-complete, EXPSPACE-complete) for LSTA properties like nonemptiness and language inclusion.
important_parameters: The size of the automaton ($|A|$), the forward-memory width ($	ext{fmw}_\pi(B)$), and the qubit order permutation ($\pi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the structure of LSTAs, specifically assuming perfect binary trees for state representation, and uses techniques like block compilation and adjoints for circuit analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate quantum states as perfect binary trees, provide examples of LSTAs recognizing specific states, and show the structure of LSTAs used in complexity proofs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining LSTAs for quantum states, establishing complexity bounds for basic properties (nonemptiness, inclusion), and then developing advanced techniques involving forward-memory width and scheduling heuristics for practical circuit verification.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical tools to determine the computational feasibility of verifying complex quantum circuits, which is crucial for scaling up quantum computation.
